claims: ProgBase AutoCal native refresh cadence is configuration-driven; it is not a fixed 75 ms loop.
The native preference key is refresh_time_ms with a default value of 300.
0x0051988C loads refresh_time_ms and stores the signed interval into TAutoCalUI +0x4A8/+0x4AC.
0x005162F8 checks elapsed time against +0x4A8/+0x4AC before performing the expensive AutoCal refresh; a force flag can bypass the early return.
The AutoCal Settings DFM exposes RefreshTime as a trackbar with Min=200, Max=2000, Position=300 and OnChange=RefreshTimeChange.
RefreshTimeChange @ 0x005141A4 reads the trackbar Position and updates LabelRefreshValue; FormClose reads the same RefreshTime.Position into the settings persistence path.
SettingsImgClick and other settings reload paths call 0x0051988C, applying the stored cadence to the live AutoCal UI.
evidence: 0x0051988C references the literal preference key refresh_time_ms with fallback/default 300 and writes the returned integer to UI +0x4A8, sign extension to +0x4AC.
0x005162F8 obtains timing state, compares it with UI +0x4A8/+0x4AC, and returns early unless the interval elapsed or the force flag is set.
DFM RefreshTime: Min=200, Max=2000, Position=300, OnChange=RefreshTimeChange; LabelRefreshValue Caption=300.
0x005141A4 reads *(RefreshTime +0x2B0) and writes the formatted value to LabelRefreshValue.
TAutoCalSettings.FormClose @ 0x00513E68 reads RefreshTime.Position as part of settings persistence.
TAutoCalUI.SettingsImgClick @ 0x00519708 calls 0x0051988C after settings dialog completion.
boundary: This proof establishes the native ProgBase scheduling contract. A 75 ms OMEGAS presentation cadence is an OMEGAS design choice unless separately tied to another original ProgBase path.
